This one is about finding things. Search knows games now: type "mario 3" or "smb3" and you get
the game, on each console, in every build that has it, and one click downloads it. There's a BIOS
search too ("ps1 bios usa"). Downloads go straight into your download folder, and there's a way to
start over when you want to test something from scratch.

**Upgrading:** replace `usnfetch.exe` and start it as usual. About 20 seconds after it starts, it
works out the game and BIOS lists of the builds you've opened before, in the background, from
the indexes it already has. Search finds them once that's done.

Categories are gone, so new downloads land in `<download folder>\<share name>`. What you
downloaded before stays where it is, in its category folder: it's still marked as already there
when you browse, and a download that was paused or failed partway carries on in its old folder.

## Search by game

- **One line per game and console.** "mario 3" gives *Mario Party 3 · Nintendo 64*, *Super Mario
  Bros. 3 · NES*, *Super Mario 3D World · Wii U*… Regions, revisions, discs and the many names one
  console goes by ("nes", "famicom", "Nintendo Entertainment System") fold into one line, with the
  builds that have it.
- **Abbreviations and numbers:** "smb3", "sm64", "ff7", "zelda 2". The closest titles come first,
  games more of your builds have a little higher, hacks lower.
- **Click a game's name to download it.** A game that's one file of up to 1 GB goes straight to
  your browser's downloads. Anything bigger, or a game of several discs or tracks, goes through
  the download queue with the usual review, all its discs together.
- Each build on the line opens that build at the game's folder, or its arrow queues the game
  from that build.
- About 180,000 games across my builds, and it answers in a few milliseconds.

## BIOS search

Pick BIOS next to the search box and type "ps1 bios usa", "ps2 bios europe", "sega cd bios" or a
file name. usnfetch knows BIOS files by name (Sony's model numbers, PS2 BIOS versions, Kickstarts
and the rest emulators look for) and by the folders they're in, so scph5501.bin shows up as
*SCPH-5501 · PlayStation · USA*. Click one to download it in your browser.

## What's inside each build

Once you've opened a build, its row in the catalog says what's in it: how many games, for which
consoles. Searching the catalog for a console finds the builds that have it, and on a build's page
each console is a chip that opens its folder.

## Starting over

- **System → Reset** wipes what you tick: the caches, what opening shares learned, health checks,
  the catalog, the download queue and history, or the settings (keeping your Usenet providers if
  you like). usnfetch restarts and does it as it starts. Downloaded files are never touched, and
  the web password always stays.
- **Forget this build**, in a share's Details, does the same for one build: its next open fetches
  everything from Usenet again, like the first time.

## Also

- **Notifications.** On Windows the tray icon tells you when a download finishes or fails.
- **Disk guard.** Downloads pause by themselves before the download drive fills up (5 GB is kept
  free unless you change it) and carry on once there's room again.
- **Show in folder** on a finished download opens it in Explorer.
- **A proper progress bar while a share opens**, a little text-mode one in your theme's colours,
  as wide as the window. The details go to the log on the System page instead.
- No more categories in the download review or in Settings.
- Search across shares looks at every file and folder of every share you've opened, when it isn't
  a game you're after.
